title: Moment of Inertia: Parallel Axis Theorem
subject: Physics
topic: Parallel axis theorem and standard moments of inertia
hook: One formula that turns 10 JEE rotation questions into 1-liners.
telegram_post: 🌀 Parallel Axis Theorem I = I_cm + Md² • Works for any body, axis must be parallel to one through the centre of mass • Rod about end: ML²/12 + M(L/2)² = ML²/3 • Ring about tangent (in plane): MR²/2 + MR² = 3MR²/2
key_points: I = I_cm + Md² for any axis parallel to an axis through the centre of mass.
d is the perpendicular distance between the two parallel axes.
I is minimum about the axis through the centre of mass.
Rod about centre: ML²/12; about end: ML²/3.
Ring: MR²; disc: MR²/2 about the central perpendicular axis.
Solid sphere: 2MR²/5; hollow sphere: 2MR²/3 about a diameter.

mcqs.question: Moment of inertia of a thin uniform rod of mass M and length L about an axis through one end, perpendicular to the rod, is:
mcqs.explanation: I = ML²/12 + M(L/2)² = ML²/3 by the parallel axis theorem.

scenes.heading: Parallel axis theorem

terms.meaning: MI about axis through centre of mass

scenes.narration: I equals I c m plus M d squared. I c m is about the centre of mass axis, and d is the distance between the two parallel axes.

scenes.heading: Use it fast
scenes.narration: Rod about its centre is M L squared by twelve, about its end it becomes M L squared by three. A solid sphere about a tangent is seven by five M R squared.

scenes.heading: Quick check
scenes.body: Rod (M, L) about one end, perpendicular. I = ?
scenes.narration: Quick check. Moment of inertia of a rod about one end?

scenes.heading: Answer: ML²/3
scenes.narration: It's M L squared by three. Twelfth plus a quarter gives one third.

notes.heading: Statement
paragraphs: The moment of inertia about any axis equals the moment of inertia about a parallel axis through the centre of mass plus Md², where d is the perpendicular distance between the axes.
bullets: Valid for any rigid body (2D or 3D).
One of the two axes must pass through the centre of mass.

notes.heading: Standard results
bullets: Ring about tangent perpendicular to plane: 2MR²
